11:1.sourceText: Ἤκουσαν δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ οἱ ὄντες κατὰ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ὅτι καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ.
11:1.targetText: And the apostles and the brothers who are in Judea heard that the nations also received the word of God,

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Judea is not separately expressed.

11:2.sourceText: Ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβη Πέτρος εἰς Ἱερουσαλήμ, διεκρίνοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς
11:2.targetText: and when Peter came up to Jerusalem, those of circumcision were contending with him,

11:3.sourceText: λέγοντες ὅτι Εἰσῆλθες πρὸς ἄνδρας ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας καὶ συνέφαγες αὐτοῖς.
11:3.targetText: saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men, and ate with them!”

groups.note: The actual construction is having uncircumcision, with a noun and having participle; English uncircumcised recasts that whole modifier without a separately printed adjective.

unmappedSource.reason: The quotation-introducing ὅτι has no separate English word before the direct speech.

11:4.sourceText: ἀρξάμενος δὲ Πέτρος ἐξετίθετο αὐτοῖς καθεξῆς λέγων
11:4.targetText: And Peter having begun, set [it] forth to them in order, saying,

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of the exposition; this verse has no separately written Greek object pronoun for it.

11:5.sourceText: Ἐγὼ ἤμην ἐν πόλει Ἰόππῃ προσευχόμενος, καὶ εἶδον ἐν ἐκστάσει ὅραμα, καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιεμένην ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἦλθεν ἄχρι ἐμοῦ·
11:5.targetText: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and I saw in a trance a vision, a certain vessel coming down, as a great sheet by four corners being let down out of Heaven, and it came to me;

groups.note: Joppa is a dative name in apposition to the dative city; English expresses the city-name relation as of Joppa, without a separately written of preposition.
The dative numeral and corners noun jointly give the lowering points, rendered by four corners; by expresses this case construction rather than a separate Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Heaven is not separately expressed.

11:6.sourceText: εἰς ἣν ἀτενίσας κατενόουν, καὶ εἶδον τὰ τετράποδα τῆς γῆς καὶ τὰ θηρία καὶ τὰ ἑρπετὰ καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
11:6.targetText: at which having looked steadfastly, I was considering, and I saw the four-footed beasts of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the creeping things, and the birds of the sky;

groups.note: The actual τετράποδα is a substantival adjective, four-footed ones, expressed as four-footed beasts; the next wild beasts is the separate written θηρία noun.

11:7.sourceText: ἤκουσα δὲ καὶ φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι Ἀναστάς, Πέτρε, θῦσον καὶ φάγε.
11:7.targetText: and I heard a voice saying to me, Having risen, Peter, slay and eat;

unmappedSource.reason: The additional καί after δέ is not separately expressed by an additional English also or and.

11:8.sourceText: εἶπον δέ Μηδαμῶς, Κύριε, ὅτι κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον οὐδέποτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ στόμα μου.
11:8.targetText: and I said, Not so, Lord, because anything common or unclean has at no time entered into my mouth;

unmappedSource.reason: The article before my mouth is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly includes πᾶν, anything, whereas pinned N1904 has the bare common/unclean nominal modifiers without that written quantifier.

11:9.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ἐκ δευτέρου φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ Ἃ ὁ Θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου.
11:9.targetText: and a voice answered me a second time out of Heaven, What God cleansed, you do not declare common.

groups.note: The actual imperative κοινοῦ is a single making-or-regarding-common predicate, expanded in English as do declare common rather than a separate Greek declaring verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Heaven and God are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional μοι, me, with answered, absent from pinned N1904.

11:10.sourceText: τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς, καὶ ἀνεσπάσθη πάλιν ἅπαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν.
11:10.targetText: And this happened three times, and again was all drawn up to Heaven,

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Heaven is not separately expressed.

11:11.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξαυτῆς τρεῖς ἄνδρες ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐν ᾗ ἦμεν, ἀπεσταλμένοι ἀπὸ Καισαρίας πρός με.
11:11.targetText: and behold, immediately, three men stood at the house in which I was, having been sent from Caesarea to me,

groups.note: The shared be predicate is linked, but both pinned N1904 tags are V-IAI-1P, we were, unlike the singular TR ἤμην. English I is separately recorded as a subject-reading gap.

unmappedTarget.reason: Both N1904 analyses give ἦμεν, first-person plural we were. The pinned TR has first-person singular ἤμην, I was, followed by English I; the number difference remains explicit.

11:12.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμά μοι συνελθεῖν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρίναντα. ἦλθον δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ καὶ οἱ ἓξ ἀδελφοὶ οὗτοι, καὶ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀνδρός.
11:12.targetText: and the Spirit said to me to go with them, doubting nothing, and these six brothers also went with me, and we entered into the house of the man,

groups.note: The actual διακρίναντα has aorist active participle analyses in the pinned source; the pinned TR instead has present middle διακρινόμενον. English doubting renders the shared διακρίνω head without claiming a middle or present source form.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before these six brothers is not separately expressed.

11:13.sourceText: ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ἡμῖν πῶς εἶδεν τὸν ἄγγελον ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ σταθέντα καὶ εἰπόντα· Ἀπόστειλον εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνα τὸν ἐπικαλούμενον Πέτρον,
11:13.targetText: he also declared to us how he saw the messenger standing in his house, and saying to him, Send men to Joppa, and call for Simon, who is surnamed Peter,

unmappedSource.reason: The article in his house is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly supplies αὐτῷ with saying; the N1904 sentence has no corresponding recipient pronoun.
The pinned TR explicitly includes ἄνδρας after send; this object noun is absent from pinned N1904.

11:14.sourceText: ὃς λαλήσει ῥήματα πρὸς σὲ ἐν οἷς σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ πᾶς ὁ οἶκός σου.
11:14.targetText: who will speak sayings by which you will be saved, you and all your house.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual πρὸς σέ, to you as the speaking recipient, is not separately expressed in this English sentence. The later you in you will be saved is the subject of the actual second-person salvation verb, not a relabeling of this speech recipient.
The article in all your house is not separately expressed.

11:15.sourceText: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἄρξασθαί με λαλεῖν ἐπέπεσεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὥσπερ καὶ ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀρχῇ.
11:15.targetText: And in my beginning to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as also on us in the beginning,

groups.note: The actual accusative με is the personal subject of the beginning infinitive, expressed as the possessive my before the English verbal noun beginning.

unmappedSource.reason: The articular beginning infinitive under English my beginning and the repeated article before Holy are not separately expressed.

11:16.sourceText: ἐμνήσθην δὲ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ Κυρίου, ὡς ἔλεγεν Ἰωάνης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι, ὑμεῖς δὲ βαπτισθήσεσθε ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ.
11:16.targetText: and I remembered the saying of the LORD, how He said, John indeed immersed in water, but you will be immersed in the Holy Spirit;

groups.note: The dative water noun expresses the means, rendered in water without a separately printed Greek in preposition.

11:17.sourceText: εἰ οὖν τὴν ἴσην δωρεὰν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς ὡς καὶ ἡμῖν, πιστεύσασιν ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ἐγὼ τίς ἤμην δυνατὸς κωλῦσαι τὸν Θεόν;
11:17.targetText: if then God gave to them the equal gift as also to us, having believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, I—how was I able to withstand God?”

groups.note: The actual τίς is a nominative personal interrogative, who or what; English how recasts the question about the speaker and his ability. It is not a printed πῶς adverb.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before God are not separately expressed.

11:18.sourceText: ἀκούσαντες δὲ ταῦτα ἡσύχασαν, καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν Θεὸν λέγοντες Ἄρα καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὁ Θεὸς τὴν μετάνοιαν εἰς ζωὴν ἔδωκεν.
11:18.targetText: And they, having heard these things, were silent, and were glorifying God, saying, “Then, indeed, God also gave conversion to life to the nations.”

groups.note: Both pinned analyses of ἐδόξασαν are aorist active indicative, unlike the TR imperfect ἐδόξαζον behind English were glorifying. The shared glorifying predicate is retained with the form difference explicit.
The actual noun is μετάνοια, change of mind or repentance, rendered conversion. This records the translation of that noun rather than an extra Greek conversion verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before God and conversion are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has the particle γε in ἄραγε; pinned N1904 has ἄρα without this additional particle.

11:19.sourceText: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες ἀπὸ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς γενομένης ἐπὶ Στεφάνῳ διῆλθον ἕως Φοινίκης καὶ Κύπρου καὶ Ἀντιοχείας, μηδενὶ λαλοῦντες τὸν λόγον εἰ μὴ μόνον Ἰουδαίοις.
11:19.targetText: Those, indeed, therefore, having been scattered abroad, from the tribulation that came after Stephen, went through to Phoenicia, and Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to none except to Jews only;

groups.note: The actual preposition is ἐπί with Stephen in the dative, a relation to the Stephen-associated tribulation, rendered after Stephen. No separately written after-death phrase or death noun is present.

11:20.sourceText: Ἦσαν δέ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες Κύπριοι καὶ Κυρηναῖοι, οἵτινες ἐλθόντες εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐλάλουν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς Ἕλληνας, εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν.
11:20.targetText: and there were certain of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who having entered into Antioch, were speaking to the Hellenists, proclaiming good news—the Lord Jesus,

groups.note: The actual Κύπριοι is an ethnic or personal designation, Cypriots; both pinned analyses record N-NPM, a noun analysis. English men of Cyprus expresses that designation without an independently printed Greek Cyprus place-name.

The actual Κυρηναῖοι is an ethnic or personal designation, Cyrenians; both pinned analyses record N-NPM, a noun analysis. English names Cyrene under the shared of construction, without an independently printed Greek Cyrene place-name.

N1904 has ἐλθόντες εἰς, having come into, while the TR has an entered compound. The actual coming participle plus its into preposition jointly anchor the English having entered into; no compound source spelling is invented.
The single εὐαγγελιζόμενοι verb expresses proclaiming good news; news is not an independent noun in the source.

unmappedSource.reason: The additional καί beside were speaking is not separately expressed as English also.
The pinned N1904 reads τοὺς Ἕλληνας, the Greeks, while the pinned TR reads τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς, Hellenists. The whole article-and-person designation remains a witness gap.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows the pinned TR Ἑλληνιστάς rather than N1904 Ἕλληνας, Greeks; these distinct designations are not conflated.

11:21.sourceText: καὶ ἦν χεὶρ Κυρίου μετ’ αὐτῶν, πολύς τε ἀριθμὸς ὁ πιστεύσας ἐπέστρεψεν ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον.
11:21.targetText: and the hand of the LORD was with them, a great number also, having believed, turned to the LORD.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before the believing participle is not separately expressed in English.

11:22.sourceText: Ἠκούσθη δὲ ὁ λόγος εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς οὔσης ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ περὶ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν Βαρνάβαν ἕως Ἀντιοχείας·
11:22.targetText: And the account was heard in the ears of the assembly that [is] in Jerusalem concerning them, and they sent forth Barnabas to go through to Antioch,

groups.note: The actual οὔσης is a present participle of εἰμί, be, rendered by the bracketed English is in that is in Jerusalem. The brackets do not erase this actual written Greek be predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has the additional διελθεῖν, to go through, absent from pinned N1904.

11:23.sourceText: ὃς παραγενόμενος καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν χάριν τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐχάρη, καὶ παρεκάλει πάντας τῇ προθέσει τῆς καρδίας προσμένειν τῷ Κυρίῳ,
11:23.targetText: who, having come, and having seen the grace of God, was glad, and was exhorting all with purpose of heart to cleave to the LORD,

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article introducing the grace-of-God modifier has no separate English word.

11:24.sourceText: ὅτι ἦν ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ πλήρης Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ πίστεως. καὶ προσετέθη ὄχλος ἱκανὸς τῷ Κυρίῳ.
11:24.targetText: because he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit, and of faith, and a great multitude was added to the LORD.

11:25.sourceText: ἐξῆλθεν δὲ εἰς Ταρσὸν ἀναζητῆσαι Σαῦλον,
11:25.targetText: And Barnabas went forth to Tarsus, to seek for Saul,

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly names Barnabas here, whereas N1904 leaves the going subject understood.

11:26.sourceText: καὶ εὑρὼν ἤγαγεν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν. ἐγένετο δὲ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ὅλον συναχθῆναι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ διδάξαι ὄχλον ἱκανόν, χρηματίσαι τε πρώτως ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τοὺς μαθητὰς Χριστιανούς.
11:26.targetText: and having found him, he brought him to Antioch, and it came to pass that they assembled together a whole year in the assembly, and taught a great multitude, and the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

groups.note: The actual dative αὐτοῖς is the personal complement of it came about, expanded as English they with the gathering/teaching infinitival complement; the source case remains dative, not nominative.
The actual συναχθῆναι is an aorist passive infinitive, be gathered together; English assembled together is an intransitive past rendering of that same gathering predicate.
The actual διδάξαι is an aorist active infinitive, recast as English past taught within the came-about complement.

The actual χρηματίσαι is an active infinitive with the lexical sense of receiving an appellation; English were called recasts this naming predicate passively, not a source passive καλέω form. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/chrematizo .

The actual named Saul at 11:25 is the same patient of the uninterrupted seeking, finding, and bringing sequence. English repeats him for finding and bringing. This shares the one original Saul identity, retaining its 11:25 link; it is not moved and no αὐτός pronoun is invented. The pinned TR independently prints additional αὐτόν objects in 11:26, which N1904 does not have.

unmappedSource.reason: The additional καί after αὐτοῖς is not separately expressed in the English sentence.

11:27.sourceText: Ἐν ταύταις δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις κατῆλθον ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων προφῆται εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν·
11:27.targetText: And in those days there came from Jerusalem prophets to Antioch,

groups.note: The actual demonstrative ταύταις is proximal these; English uses the retrospective those for the same days, not a different printed Greek demonstrative.

unmappedSource.reason: The article with those days is not separately expressed.

11:28.sourceText: ἀναστὰς δὲ εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος ἐσήμαινεν διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος λιμὸν μεγάλην μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν οἰκουμένην· ἥτις ἐγένετο ἐπὶ Κλαυδίου.
11:28.targetText: and one of them, by name Agabus, having stood up, signified through the Spirit a great scarcity is about to be throughout all the world—which also came to pass in the time of Claudius Caesar—

groups.note: The actual λιμός is the famine or food-scarcity noun, rendered scarcity; this is not a Greek word for a generic shortage with a different lexical identity.

The actual μέλλειν and following ἔσεσθαι are infinitives; the latter is future be. English is about to be renders that infinitival future construction without replacing the source with an indicative form.
The actual ἐπί with the personal name Claudius expresses the time under that ruler, expanded as in the time of; time is not an independently printed Greek noun here.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR prints an additional καί before the fulfillment verb; it is absent from pinned N1904.
The pinned TR includes Καίσαρος after Claudius, absent from pinned N1904.

11:29.sourceText: τῶν δὲ μαθητῶν καθὼς εὐπορεῖτό τις, ὥρισαν ἕκαστος αὐτῶν εἰς διακονίαν πέμψαι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἀδελφοῖς·
11:29.targetText: and the disciples, according as anyone was prospering, determined each of them to send for ministry to the brothers dwelling in Judea,

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Judea is not separately expressed.

11:30.sourceText: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησαν ἀποστείλαντες πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους διὰ χειρὸς Βαρνάβα καὶ Σαύλου.
11:30.targetText: which also they did, having sent to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
